title: In and out parameters
recap: Input parameters supply data; output parameters receive calculated results; in/out parameters do both. Non-const references can represent output destinations, but the contract must specify what happens on failure.
Validate before changing any output when failure promises to preserve state. This makes callers able to inspect the status without recovering partially updated results.
objectives: Implement the stated behavior for multiple inputs.
Run the visible tests and explain one boundary case.
warnings: The function/type interface is fixed, but implementation syntax is your choice.
Do not remove the visible tests; the checker keeps an independent copy.
Respect the stated input domain and lifetime/range rules.
challenge: Implement divideWithRemainder(numerator,denominator,quotient,remainder). If denominator is zero, return false and leave both output integers unchanged. Otherwise write the C++ integer quotient and remainder, and return true. Output references refer to distinct objects. Inputs are small, avoiding division overflow.
hints: Write both outputs only on success.
C++ remainder follows the numerator sign for these inputs.
